Modern.brandNameRationale: Three words. Steam names the most basic spa element. & Co. closes it as a small modern operation. The brand sits on the most ancient bathing tradition (steam) and frames it as a modern small business.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern spas have moved past the candles-and-music aesthetic. Customers are design-literate and willing to pay for a real bathing experience without the wellness theatre. The opening is a spa brand that looks like a hotel, operates like a clinic, and feels like a public bath.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Bathhouse (bathhouse.com) holds the modern New York peer position. Othership (othership.us) sits in the contrast-bathing tier. WORLD SPA (worldspa.com) does the Brooklyn middle. We sit closer to Bathhouse in posture.
Modern.positioningStatement: A modern bathhouse with real heat and no wellness theatre.

targetAudience.primary: 28 to 50. Lives in a city. Goes to a spa once a month. Tired of the candles-and-music aesthetic. Wants real saunas, real cold plunges, and a real attendant.

dos: Show the temperatures and times clearly
Talk to the customer as an adult

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark only. STEAM & CO. in a soft modern grotesk, all caps, three words on one line. A small geometric mark, three thin vertical lines suggesting rising steam, used as the favicon and on the locker key.

typography.primary: GT America for the wordmark and headlines
typography.secondary: GT America Mono for time-and-temperature data
typography.rationale: One family. The mono carries the temperatures, times, and prices. The regular carries the brand.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No candles. No piped music. No essential oil diffusers. No celebrity wellness partnerships. No 'mind-body journey' copy.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: A bathhouse with the sauna temperature posted on the door. A printed bathing protocol card given to every first-timer. A monthly newsletter with bathing notes from the staff. No social media beyond a single archive.

Luxury.brandNameRationale: Two words. The Thermal names the older European tradition of bathing at natural hot springs. The definite article makes it sound like an institution, a destination, a place clients return to over decades.
Luxury.story: The Thermal was founded around an existing natural hot spring. The current operators have stayed at the same source. The bathing protocol has stayed close to the original. Some clients have been bathing at the spring for two generations.
Luxury.industrySummary: Top end spa and bathing has been moving toward larger destination resorts and bigger programs. There's a parallel market for small heritage thermal baths in the older European tradition. Few guests, old protocols, lasting relationships. The customer is paying for the spring, the protocol, and the next visit in a year.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Therme Vals (therme-vals.ch) holds the institutional thermal-bath peer position. Aman Resorts spa programs (aman.com) sit in the destination-luxury tier. Friedrichsbad (friedrichsbad.eu) does the heritage European thermal middle. We belong in their company.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A small heritage thermal bath with a fixed protocol and a long client book.

targetAudience.primary: Wealthy. Often inherited. Travels to bathe. Books the same destination annually. Values the protocol and the silence more than the amenities.

dos: Speak in the language of bathing tradition

Luxury.logoDirection: A classical serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small hand-drawn wave-line hallmark, two thin curves suggesting steam over water, used on the locker key, the printed protocol card, and the brass plaque outside the bath.

colorPalette.name: Stone Grey
colorPalette.meaning: Bathing-room stone, the column of an old thermal.

colorPalette.name: Thermal Green
colorPalette.meaning: Deep mineral pool, the moss on the rocks.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.secondary: Söhne for the secure booking portal
typography.rationale: A high contrast classical serif sets the heritage tone. A modern grotesk handles the few digital surfaces.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No public day-passes. No third-party booking platforms. No press tour. No social media presence. No spa packages.

Minimal.brandNameRationale: Single word. Soak is the smallest verb of bathing. The brand sits on the most basic act of being in water. Plain, direct, immediately understood.
Minimal.industrySummary: Most spa brands have elaborate names suggesting wellness, journey, or transformation. There's an opening for one that strips it back to the verb itself.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Most spa brands fail this purity test. The closest peers in spirit are some Japanese onsen traditions (where the spring, not the brand, does the work) and certain Korean bathhouse aesthetics.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A bathhouse with a soaking tub and an hour. Nothing else.

targetAudience.primary: Adults who want to soak in hot water and don't need a relationship with the spa. They want the water, the silence, the towel.

dos: Show the bath, the temperature, the price
Confirm the booking in one line

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. SOAK in a single weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps, four letters with generous space. No icon. The booking confirmation, the locker key, and the towel tag all carry the wordmark and nothing else.

typography.rationale: One face. The booking, the locker key, and the receipt all carry the same wordmark.

customSections.title: Not this
customSections.body: No spa packages. No subscription model. No retail products. No newsletter. No social media presence.

Corporate.brandNameRationale: Three words. Lakeside suggests a destination location and quiet hospitality. Spa Group names the holding-company category. The whole name reads like a real, established spa operator already on the panel at hotel real estate investors and hospitality groups.
Corporate.industrySummary: Spa operations within hospitality is a serious B2B category. Hotel owners, resort operators, and destination wellness investors need operators who can run spa programs at scale with consistent service standards and reporting. The category is dominated by the major hotel groups' in-house operations and a few specialist firms.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Six Senses (sixsenses.com) holds the integrated luxury-spa peer position. Aman Resorts (aman.com) sits at the top tier. WTS International (wtsinternational.com) does the spa-management middle. We sit smaller and more focused on the contemporary boutique-hotel side.
Corporate.positioningStatement: Spa operations and management for boutique hotels and destination resorts.
Corporate.positioningRationale: Boutique hotel owners want spa partners who can deliver consistent service standards without the brand baggage of the major hotel-spa groups. We sit between the major chains and the in-house operations.

targetAudience.primary: Hotel owners, real estate investors, and resort operators with hospitality holdings. They sign multi-year operating contracts for spa management.
motivations: Reliable spa operations with property-level attention
Service standards that fit the property, not a chain template
Reporting that holds up under investor scrutiny

dos: Show case studies with property-level performance
Speak to the hotel owner, not the spa guest
donts: Promote individual spa locations on social

messagingPillars.name: Property-level operations
messagingPillars.description: Each spa keeps its own identity. We operate behind the scenes.

messagingPillars.name: Service standards that travel
messagingPillars.description: Centralized training and standards across properties without a chain feel.

messagingPillars.name: Owner-aligned reporting
messagingPillars.description: Monthly P&L, quarterly performance reviews, and ESG-aligned reporting for hospitality investors.

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark to the left. The mark is a single horizontal wave reduced to two parallel curves. Reads cleanly on a procurement deck, name badge, and investor pitch book.

typography.primary: Inter for marketing and B2B materials
typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed quarterly reports
typography.rationale: Inter scales clean across digital. The serif handles formal quarterly business reviews and printed property portfolios.

customSections.title: What it doesn't do
customSections.body: No consumer-facing spa brand. No loyalty programs. No celebrity spa partnerships. The firm sells through hotel owner and investor channels, not consumer wellness.

Creative.brandNameRationale: Two words. Wet Room is the literal architectural term for a spa room (and the bathroom slang for the same idea). The brand sits on the most physical part of bathing: the wet, dripping, slightly awkward reality. Loud, warm, and slightly self-aware.
Creative.manifesto: Most spa brands sell the candle, the music, the curated journey. We made Wet Room because the actual experience of spa is wet, loud (sometimes), and physical. The cold plunge gasp. The sauna sweat. The robe that doesn't quite cover the shoulders. The brand is for the people who actually want to bathe, not to be calmed at.
Creative.industrySummary: Spa branding has been calm, candle-lit, and slightly precious. There's room for a brand that's loud, warm, sticker-friendly, and serious about the actual physical bathing experience.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Othership (othership.us) holds the loud contrast-bathing peer position. Bathhouse (bathhouse.com) sits in the modern bathhouse tier. WORLD SPA (worldspa.com) does the Brooklyn middle. We sit warmer and louder than any of them.
Creative.positioningStatement: A bathhouse for people who would rather sweat than meditate.

targetAudience.primary: 25 to 45. Goes to a bathhouse monthly. Values the heat and the cold and the physical extreme. Wants the spa to be honest about being a wet room.

dos: Make jokes about the cold plunge
Talk like the friend who is already in the sauna

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a punchy display serif with the O of ROOM stylized as a small steam circle, suggesting heat. Standalone steam-O icon for locker keys, stickers, and social profiles.

colorPalette.name: Steam Pink
colorPalette.meaning: The skin after a hot soak.
colorPalette.usage: Primary brand color, hero surfaces, social

typography.primary: Migra for the wordmark and big display
typography.secondary: PP Neue Montreal for body and locker signage
typography.rationale: Migra has warmth. Neue Montreal handles the practical bits. The pair feels designed and human.

customSections.title: What it isn't
customSections.body: Not a candle-and-music spa. Not a wellness journey. Not afraid of pink. Not too cool to celebrate the gasp from the cold plunge.

customSections.title: Where it lives
customSections.body: A bathhouse with the temperature posted on the door. A printed protocol card given to first-timers, written like a friend explaining the rules. Stickers in the lockers. A merch line of two robes and one tee that says WET ROOM across the back.
